\[
g_C = \frac{\bar m}{m_C},
\quad
\bar m = \frac{m_R + m_G + m_B}{3},
\quad
C' = \begin{cases} \operatorname{srgb}\left(g_C \operatorname{lin}(C)\right) & \text{linear light} \\ g_C\, C & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m_C\): The mean of channel C over the image
- \(\bar m\): The mean of the three channel means
- \(g_C\): The gain of channel C

m_C is the mean of channel C over the whole image. Buchsbaum's gray-world assumption says that the average color of a scene is gray. So any difference between the channel means is taken to come from the light, and the gains remove it. After the gains, the three means are equal. With Linear light on, the default, the gains act on linear light values: decoded from sRGB, scaled, and encoded again. A change in the color of the light scales linear values, so this is the physical model. With it off, the gains scale the encoded values. A channel with mean 0 gets gain 1.
